claim: Hardware wallets keep private keys offline and are commonly considered safer than online storage (premise of the 'katanya' myth hook).
Singapore police found Ledger hardware wallets bought from some retail stores in Singapore that contained malicious hardware components able to capture recovery phrases / private keys.
According to Ledger (Donjon), the implant reads the 24-word recovery phrase and sends it out over the mobile network (LTE, provisioned eSIM).
Police received at least 2 reports since 10 Sep 2026; combined losses S$3,5 juta (~Rp49,5 miliar).
numbers: 2 cases · S$3,5 juta · Rp49,5 miliar (CNBC conversion) · since 10 Sep 2026

claim: Ledger's built-in integrity / genuine checks cannot detect the implant, because it does not modify the Secure Element or the OS.
Mid-October, Ledger asked resellers/distributors to halt sales in 7 Asian countries/territories incl. Indonesia (Singapore, Indonesia, Malaysia, Thailand, Philippines, Vietnam, Hong Kong).
numbers: 7 · 13 Oct (Malay Mail) / 14 Oct (CNBC); script says 'pertengahan Oktober' in captions only

claim: Ledger says its own infrastructure, services and direct sales channel are safe (captions).

Ledger's advice to buyers from the affected reseller in the last 90 days: don't set up unused devices; if already set up, move assets to a new signer with a new seed. Police: move remaining assets to a new trusted wallet with a newly generated recovery phrase; never share recovery phrase (captions).
An on-chain analyst (Specter, @SpecterAnalyst) estimated total losses above US$86 juta (~Rp1,5 T per CNBC); not confirmed by Ledger.
numbers: >US$86 juta · ~Rp1,5 T · estimate dated 9 Oct 2026 (Bitquery later cited US$93,2 juta, not used)
